Not exactly full as a Bourke Street tram out here.
Reckon we've earned a parma after this one.
Melbourne gets four seasons in one day. Space only has the one: cold.
Hook turn? No thanks. Out here we turn however we like.

ChitChat_Aussie: Fun fact for you: in Victoria a pot is a small beer, about two hundred and eighty-five millilitres. A schooner is the bigger one.
In Melbourne it's a parma. In Sydney it's a parmi. A chicken parmigiana by any name. Argue about it at your own risk.
Melbourne's hook turn lets you turn right from the left lane, to stay out of the way of the trams. Very clever. Very confusing for visitors.
A Victorian says bathers. Other states say togs or cozzie. I'm told it's a serious matter.
A milk bar in Victoria is a local corner shop. It sells a lot more than milk.
Yeah nah means no. Nah yeah means yes. I did not make these rules.
Arvo is afternoon. Brekkie is breakfast. Aussies shorten everything. It's efficient. I respect it.
A servo is a service station and an esky is a cooler box. I'm learning the language, one word at a time.
Prep is the first year of school in Victoria. In New South Wales they call it kindergarten.
In Victoria it's a drink tap. In New South Wales it's a bubbler. Both are just a water fountain.
Full as a goog means you've eaten far too much. A goog is an egg.
Chaddy is Chadstone, the biggest shopping centre in Australia, and it's in Melbourne. I'd get lost for a week.
A yewy is a U-turn. Chuck a yewy, as they say.
The G is the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Footy final day is basically a religious experience.
Myki is the card you tap on trams, trains and buses in Melbourne. Don't forget to top it up.
Carn is short for come on. You'll hear it at every footy ground in Melbourne.
A galah is a pink and grey cockatoo, and also what Aussies call someone being a bit silly. Not you, of course.
The Melbourne Cup is on the first Tuesday in November. They call it the race that stops a nation.
On election day in Australia there's a democracy sausage: a sausage sizzle outside the polling booth. Very civilised.
Woop Woop means a faraway, middle-of-nowhere place. Honestly, that's most of the galaxy.
A sausage is a snag, and a sausage sizzle is a barbecue fundraiser. Every Aussie has been to one.
Heaps means a lot. Reckon means think. G'day means hello. You're basically fluent already, mate.
